blockers.title: The selector decision no longer binds the change set or either compared source tree
blockers.subjectEvidence: v3's selectorDecision inputsDigest covered the ownership record, dependency edges, trigger table, and change set. v4 correctly removes the trigger table but replaces the field with only the ownership-record digest and DR-103 dependency-edge digest. The newly named previousCommittedTree says it is digest-pinned at execution, yet neither that digest, the current tree/candidate identity, nor a canonical changedUnits digest appears in selectorDecision or independent-release evidence.
blockers.counterexample: Keep the ownership record and dependency graph unchanged. Commit X changes component A and emits a selectorDecision selecting A. Commit Y changes component B. Because both decisions have the same specified inputsDigest and selectorDecision carries no source-tree or change-set identity, X's decision can be replayed with A's signed lane evidence while B is skipped. The durable evidence shape cannot prove that its selected/skipped partition was computed from Y rather than X.
blockers.whyBlocking: Selected-lane explanations and skipped-lane proofs are the exact evidence for the no-affected-omitted-lane rule. If they are not cryptographically joined to the source comparison that generated changedUnits, a stale or substituted decision can certify under-selection without triggering ambiguity. This is a v4 regression at the release-evidence boundary.
blockers.requiredRepair: Include a canonical change-set digest in selectorDecision.inputsDigest that binds the current candidate tree/commit, the authoritative comparison baseline, and the normalized add/delete/rename/byte-change set. Join that decision digest to every signed lane emission and aggregate/release evidence. Keep the trigger table removed; do not solve this by restoring it.

blockers.title: Removing the trigger table left an undefined trigger rule and no authoritative multi-component-to-shared-lane selection path
blockers.subjectEvidence: The authority and selectorDecision now say there is no trigger table. The algorithm seeds SL-2/SL-3/SL-4 only from directly changed PROTOCOL/SEMANTIC/LOCK-owned units, then propagates shared surface to consumers and reverse dependencies. It contains no rule from a selected set of multiple components back to those shared lanes. Nevertheless G16-5 says those lanes produce results when selected because the selector includes more than one component or a protocol/lock/authority surface, and skippedLaneProof still invokes an undefined 'trigger' rule. honestyRepairsFromV3 falsely says the skipped-proof trigger was removed; the recursive delta confirms that path did not change.
blockers.counterexample: Change a unit owned by B while A declares a dependency on B. The closed algorithm selects B and then A at the joint fixpoint, but no shared surface was selected, so it skips SL-2, SL-3, and SL-4. That contradicts G16-5's multi-component selection cause. Selecting the lanes instead requires an unenumerated trigger rule that is absent from the ownership digest, custody, completeness, self-change, algorithm, and selectorDecision inputs.
blockers.whyBlocking: The design contract has no single lawful result for a mandatory cross-component acceptance case: obeying the closed selector under-selects relative to G16-5, while satisfying G16-5 invents the second authority MCICV3-B1 required removing. The residual trigger also prevents a skipped-lane proof from being derived only from the declared authority set.
blockers.requiredRepair: Decide the intended cross-component rule explicitly. If multiple selected components must select shared lanes, encode exact component-set-to-lane edges or predicates inside the custodied ownership record, include them in completeness/self-change/digests, and iterate them in the fixpoint. If that is not intended, remove the multi-component cause from G16-5. In either case replace 'trigger' in skippedLaneProof with the exact declared relation and roster every changed path.

shouldFix.title: The named first-parent baseline still omits earlier commits in a multi-commit candidate
shouldFix.measurement: previousCommittedTree is now named as the immediate first parent of 'the change under test', but the contract does not require that change to be an integration merge commit or require evidence from every candidate commit. Evaluating an ordinary multi-commit branch head against its first parent sees only the final commit. The identity/claim union in comparisonBasis stabilizes the lane universe; it does not restore source units absent from that diff.
shouldFix.counterexample: A two-commit candidate changes component A in commit 1 and component B in commit 2. A head-only run compares commit 2 with commit 1, selects B, and lawfully skips A because the A unit never enters changedUnits. No ambiguity rule fires.
shouldFix.suggestedFix: Define a vendor-neutral whole-candidate comparison: for example, integration-target merge base to candidate tree, with the normalized union of all candidate changes. Pin both endpoints and specify merge/rewrite behavior. If every commit is instead authoritative, require the complete ordered set of per-commit decisions and their aggregate union.

shouldFix.title: G16-3 assigns two outcome laws to one composite corpus change-class cell
shouldFix.measurement: C-CONFLICT-OWNER still means 'more than one owner or an owner outside the universe'. G16-3 locally narrows C-CONFLICT-OWNER to multiple owners, where complete-universe over-selection is allowed, while separately requiring REFUSE for an out-of-universe owner. The matrix requires a result per changeClass, not a distinct result for each side of an 'or', and missing component/incomplete-universe cases are also absent from changeClasses.
shouldFix.risk: A harness can populate the one C-CONFLICT-OWNER cell with the multiple-owner branch and never demonstrate the out-of-universe REFUSE branch, while still claiming matrix completeness. The repaired prose is safe, but the executable hostile-corpus partition is not closed enough to prove it.
shouldFix.suggestedFix: Split the corpus into distinct C-MULTIPLE-OWNERS and C-OWNER-OUTSIDE-UNIVERSE classes with exact expected results. Add distinct missing-component-declaration and incomplete-universe classes, or explicitly require all named subcases within every matrix cell.

verdictBasis: 2 blockers, 3 SHOULD-FIX, 1 advisory. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX; the gate is not met.
verdictStatement: v4 repairs the direct selectorDecision/ID-DEP-C6 trigger-table references, joint propagation fixpoint, REFUSE-only outcome prose, predecessor-advisory booking, and IR non-pass semantics. It remains non-acceptable because selector evidence no longer binds the change set and because the removed trigger table leaves G16-5's multi-component shared-lane selection without an authoritative rule. The first-parent baseline, composite G16-3 corpus class, and unrostered reMeasurementAtV4 addition also remain SHOULD-FIX.

authorityOfThisVerdict.note: Independent measurement only. DR-121 remains OPEN and G16 remains not QUALIFIED; coordinator disposition is separate.

coordinatorNote: REJECT at 2 blockers / 3 SHOULD-FIX / 1 advisory. Bind selector decisions to the canonical source change set and both comparison endpoints; replace the undefined cross-component trigger with one custodied rule consistent with G16-5; define a whole-candidate baseline; split the hostile owner/universe corpus cases; and roster reMeasurementAtV4. DR-121 remains OPEN, G16 remains not QUALIFIED, no implementation is authorized, and no D-096 (A) grant is minted.
